aldo-pena.title: Aldo Peña — Digital Artist Archive
aldo-pena.description: UX/UI design and frontend development of a digital artist archive to preserve, organise and explore artworks, career history and documentation.

hero.title: Aldo Peña — Digital Artist Archive
hero.subtitle: UX/UI design and frontend development of a digital platform to preserve, organise and make Aldo Peña’s work, career and legacy accessible.

origin.title: From showcasing artworks to organising an artist’s career.
origin.content: The project began as a website to bring together and showcase Aldo Peña’s work. The variety of material —artworks, teaching, professional practice and historical documentation— led to a broader proposal for a digital archive.

context.problema: Artworks, professional projects and biographical information need different forms of presentation. The challenge was to define the sections and detail views each type of content required and make them easy to explore.
context.objetivo: Enable visitors to browse artworks by category, consult their images and metadata, and explore the artist’s career and professional practice. The archive is intended for the following audiences:
usuario: People interested in the artist’s work and career
Researchers and people working in the arts and cultural sector
People who need to explore a large archive while keeping their place in the navigation

decisiones: Separate artworks from professional practice, with their own categories and detail views.
Provide categories and sorting for browsing artworks.
Present artwork details in a modal with images, metadata, and previous and next navigation.
Separate data queries from interface components and use external image storage.

sitemap.title: Architecture for an extensive career
sitemap.description: Navigation separates Biography, Works, Practice, and Legacy and Archive. Within Works and Practice, categories lead from an overview to individual artworks and projects. Legacy and Archive remains a section awaiting content.

interaction.title: Explore the work while keeping its context
interaction.description: Visitors can choose a category and sort artworks by date, title or featured status. The load-more control increases the number of visible pieces. Opening an artwork displays its details in a modal and reflects the selection in the URL.

responsive.title: React and Supabase: from data model to interface
responsive.description: The React interface queries Supabase to retrieve archive data. Each artwork is linked to its category, images and exhibition records. Image files are served from Supabase Storage. The Practice section has its own queries for projects and documentation.

artworkExperience.title: Explore a piece without leaving the archive
artworkExperience.description: Each artwork can be explored in a modal within the archive. Visitors can browse images, move to the previous or next artwork, and consult the available metadata. The selected artwork is reflected in the URL so a direct link to that piece can be shared.
artworkExperience.alt: Painting detail with an image gallery, technique, dimensions and navigation between artworks

result.title: Current state of the archive
result.content: The implementation includes an artwork archive with categories and sorting, artwork details with images and metadata, and a multidisciplinary practice section with projects and associated documentation. Artwork and practice queries are connected to Supabase. The archive remains in development: the Legacy and Archive section currently displays a coming-soon page.

learnings: Designing for large volumes of content means thinking about relationships and architecture before screens.
Separating data, logic and presentation allows an interface to evolve independently of the archive’s final size.
In a cultural archive, interaction should support exploration without visually competing with the artwork.

practiceShowcase.title: Professional practice on mobile
practiceShowcase.description: The Practice page presents the artist’s interdisciplinary work. These views show its introduction and the Curatorial and Exhibition Design section, with access to its categories.

equinox.title: Equinox — Corporate Website Redesign
equinox.description: UX/UI design and frontend development of the Equinox corporate website, from Figma designs to React implementation.

hero.title: Equinox — Corporate Website Redesign
hero.subtitle: Redesign and frontend implementation of a B2B website presenting Equinox’s services and helping visitors contact the company.

context.problema: The brief was to visually modernise an old WordPress website and rebuild it. The initial scope did not include adding features or retaining existing functionality.
context.objetivo: Redesign the corporate presentation and build the Home, About and Contact pages for desktop and mobile.

result.title: A redesigned website, now live
result.content: Equinox’s rebuilt corporate website is live, with Home, About and Contact adapted for desktop and mobile. My contribution covered the process from the initial wireframes to the published React interface.

equinoxCase.constraintsTitle: Designing with only the existing logo
equinoxCase.constraintsText: The only supplied asset was the logo from the previous website. Without brand guidelines or company photography, I developed the visual proposal and selected Unsplash images to accompany the content.
equinoxCase.briefText: Before designing, I asked about the audience, the website’s objective, its content, the freedom to reorganise it and how to handle Contact within the agreed scope.
equinoxCase.designText: The Home structure introduces services first, followed by the company’s capabilities, About and contact. Following the first presentation, I replaced the outlined service cards with columns and icons in response to company feedback. In the visual design, capabilities are grouped on a shared background, and the green from the logo appears in icons and calls to action.
equinoxCase.mobileTitle: The structure was also planned for mobile
equinoxCase.mobileText: The mobile wireframe already shows stacked calls to action, a services carousel and single-column content blocks. The second image shows the implemented mobile interface.
equinoxCase.developmentText: I developed Home, About and Contact in React. Navigation connects the three pages and provides direct access to services from Home. On mobile, the interface includes an expandable menu, stacked calls to action and a services carousel.
equinoxCase.supportTitle: View the About and Contact wireframes
equinoxCase.supportText: The inner pages were also explored through wireframes. Contact presents email, phone and address details without a form. The contact details visible in these sketches are placeholders.
